Compile and install a Zig-backed package, and report the first errors

Source: R/build.R
build_zig.Rd

Runs the checks of rzig_status(), then installs a copy of the package with R CMD INSTALL into a library, using the Zig compiler reported by find_zig(). The complete installation log is kept, and the errors of the Zig compiler, the C compiler, the linker and the load test are extracted with their files and lines, so a failed build names its cause instead of the bare "non-zero exit status" of utils::install.packages().

Usage

build_zig(
  path,
  lib = NULL,
  preflight = TRUE,
  optimize = Sys.getenv("RZIG_OPTIMIZE", "ReleaseSafe")
)

Arguments

path

Path to the package root.

lib

The library to install into. By default a new library in the session temporary directory; library() then needs lib.loc = build$library.

preflight

If TRUE, run the checks of rzig_status() first and stop before compiling when one of them fails.

optimize

The optimize mode of the Zig code: "ReleaseSafe" (optimized, with Zig's safety checks) or "Debug" (unoptimized, with the same safety checks and complete stack traces, for debugging). The default is the environment variable RZIG_OPTIMIZE, which the generated Makevars also read, or "ReleaseSafe". The modes without safety checks (ReleaseFast, ReleaseSmall) are not available, because the boundary turns failed checks into R errors; @setRuntimeSafety(false) removes the checks of a single function.

Value

An object of class rzig_build: a list with ok (logical), package, step ("preflight", "configure", "compile", "link", "load", "install" or NA on success), errors (a data frame with the columns file, line, column, message and function_name), problems (failed checks before compilation), library, zig (the rzig_compiler used), optimize, seconds and log (the complete output of R CMD INSTALL). A failed build also signals a warning.

Details

The package is built from a copy in the session temporary directory, so the package source receives no object files or compiler caches. The installation needs a supported Zig compiler and the C toolchain of R. A package that is already loaded in the R session keeps its old native code until R restarts; the printed result says so.

Examples

package_path <- tempfile("rzig-build-", tmpdir = tempdir())
dir.create(package_path)
writeLines(c("Package: examplepkg", "Version: 0.0.1"),
  file.path(package_path, "DESCRIPTION"))
use_rzig(package_path)
#> Generated RZig bindings for examplepkg: 1 exported function
#> Created RZig scaffold for package examplepkg

# A change to main.zig without document() is caught before compiling.
main <- file.path(package_path, "src", "rzig", "src", "main.zig")
cat("/// @export\npub fn twice(x: f64) f64 {\n    return 2 * x;\n}\n",
  file = main, append = TRUE)
result <- suppressWarnings(build_zig(package_path))
result
#> Build of package examplepkg: not started; checks before compilation failed
#>   Bindings: out of date: manifest.zig, R/rzig-wrappers.R, NAMESPACE,
#>     man/twice.Rd; run document()

# With a supported Zig compiler, the regenerated package compiles; the
# compilation takes several seconds.
# \donttest{
if (isTRUE(find_zig(required = FALSE)$supported)) {
  document(package_path)
  result <- build_zig(package_path)
  result
}
#> Generated RZig bindings for examplepkg: 2 exported functions
#> Build of package examplepkg: succeeded in 11.5 seconds
#> Zig compiler: /home/runner/work/_temp/9e0fe227-0da4-4767-900a-44012cf37f43/zig-x86_64-linux-0.16.0/zig (version 0.16.0)
#> Installed into a library in the session temporary directory
# }
unlink(package_path, recursive = TRUE)
